name: Sprynt Forge — File Generation Skill
description: How to generate downloadable files (DOCX, PDF, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, code files, ZIP archives) with the Sprynt Forge tools. ALWAYS load and follow this skill whenever the user asks to create, make, export, save, write, or download any document, report, letter, presentation, deck, slides, spreadsheet, table-as-file, invoice, summary-as-a-file, or archive — even if they do not name a file format. Also load it when the user mentions document templates/styles or saving files into a collection or knowledge base.
content:
Sprynt Forge — File Generation Skill

You have three Sprynt Forge tools: create_file, create_archive, list_templates. Every successful call returns a download link. Always show that link to the user as a markdown link. Never claim a file was created without actually calling a tool.

Step 1 — Pick the format
report, letter, article, editable document → docx
polished / printable / shareable document → pdf (default for prose when unspecified)
presentation, deck, slides → pptx
table, data, budget, tracker → xlsx (default for tabular data)
plain data exchange → csv
notes, code, config → txt, md, py, json, html, xml
multiple files requested → ONE create_archive call (ZIP), never several create_file calls
Step 2 — Build the content correctly

docx / pdf → content is markdown:

# ## ### headings, - bullets, 1. numbered lists
**bold**, *italic*, `code`, fenced ``` code blocks
Tables as GitHub-style markdown tables (first row = header row)
Write the COMPLETE document. Never use "..." or placeholder text.

xlsx → content is a JSON string (NOT wrapped in code fences):

Single sheet: [["Name","Qty","Price"],["Apples",3,1.5]] — first row becomes the styled header
Multi-sheet: [{"title":"Sales","content":[[...]]},{"title":"Costs","content":[[...]]}]
Pass numbers as numbers so formulas work. No currency symbols inside number cells.

pptx → content is a JSON string:

[{"title":"Slide title","content":["bullet 1","bullet 2"],"table":[["A","B"],["1","2"]]}] (table optional)
Or markdown where each #/## heading starts a new slide
3–6 short bullets per slide. Set the title parameter to get a title slide.

csv → JSON matrix string or raw CSV text.

Placeholders usable anywhere in content and title: {{date}}, {{time}}, {{year}}, {{author}}, {{title}}.

Step 3 — Set the right parameters
filename: meaningful name with extension, e.g. q3_report.pdf
title: document heading / title slide — use it for real documents
template: ONLY when the user asks for a style. Call list_templates to see valid names. Never invent template names.
collection: ONLY when the user explicitly asks to save/store the file into a collection or knowledge base. It auto-creates if missing. Report the collection status from the tool result back to the user.
Archives

files_json for create_archive is a JSON array string; each item supports the same fields as create_file:

json
[
  {"format":"docx","filename":"report.docx","title":"Report","content":"# ..."},
  {"format":"xlsx","filename":"data.xlsx","content":[["A","B"],[1,2]]}
]

The ZIP link is returned; if a collection is given, the individual files (not the zip) are added to it.

Errors
Result starts with "Error" → the input was malformed (usually invalid JSON in content / files_json). Fix and retry ONCE.
Collection note says it failed → still deliver the download link, and tell the user the collection issue in one sentence.
Never do
Never wrap xlsx/pptx JSON in markdown code fences inside the parameter.
Never split one multi-file request into repeated create_file calls.
Never omit the returned download link from your reply.
Never set collection or template speculatively.
